reports.title: REPORT OF FOREIGN PRIVATE ISSUER PURSUANT TO RULE 13a-16 OR 15d-16 UNDER THE SECURITIES EXCHANGE ACT OF 1934
REPORT OF FOREIGN PRIVATE ISSUER PURSUANT TO RULE 13a-16 OR 15d-16 UNDER THE SECURITIES EXCHANGE ACT OF 1934

desk.period: Q3 2026 (quarter to 30 Sep 2026; results published 28 Oct 2026)
desk.headline: Operating income more than doubled to $11.95bn but adjusted EPS of $1.20 missed; 2026 production growth guidance raised to ~4%

other.label: Cash flow from operations after tax

results: Net operating income more than doubled to $11.95bn from $5.27bn as higher oil and gas prices met higher output; adjusted operating income was $12.35bn.
Adjusted EPS was $1.20, below the $1.35 estimate; net income was $2.54bn ($2.86bn adjusted).
Production rose 2% to 2,166 mboe/d, with international growth from Adura (UK) and Bacalhau (Brazil); Norway was stable and the Mongstad refinery had a record quarter.
Cash flow from operations after tax was $8.14bn and the net debt ratio fell to 3.8% from 10.4% at end-June.
Dividend of $0.39 a share; a fourth buyback tranche of up to $1.125bn started 29 Oct, completing up to $3bn for 2026 (265,300 shares bought on 29–30 Oct).

guidance.summary: Equinor raised its 2026 oil and gas production growth guidance to about 4% from 3%. On the call, as reported, organic capex stays at about $13bn for the year.

points: CFO Torgrim Reitan called Europe's gas market "tight and vulnerable", with storage at its lowest since 2011 and LNG flows through Hormuz limited.
At forward prices, 2026 operating cash flow should be about $29bn, against a $25bn base case.
From 2027 buybacks will be announced quarterly, at $2–4bn a year if Brent is $60–80 and European gas $7–11; dividends stay the first priority.
Johan Sverdrup output is down 11% this year and the decline should steepen in 2027, though 2027 output is still expected above 2025.
Empire Wind is about 80% complete, with first power planned for the first half of 2027.
call.source: Call coverage: The Stock Observer, 28 Oct 2026; Oilprice.com, 28 Oct 2026

watch: Large Norwegian tax payments in Q4 and their effect on net debt.
European gas prices and storage into winter.
The first quarterly buyback announcement under the 2027 framework.
